To solve the problem of finding the number of 10-letter strings composed of A's and B's that do not have more than 3 adjacent identical letters, we use a recurrence relation approach. We define \( S(n, r) \) as the number of n-length strings ending with a run of \( r \) identical letters (where \( r \) can be 1, 2, or 3). The total number of valid strings of length \( n \) is the sum \( S(n, 1) + S(n, 2) + S(n, 3) \).

The recurrence relations are:
- \( S(n, 1) = S(n-1, 1) + S(n-1, 2) + S(n-1, 3) \)
- \( S(n, 2) = S(n-1, 1) \)
- \( S(n, 3) = S(n-1, 2) \)

The base cases are:
- \( S(1, 1) = 2 \), \( S(1, 2) = 0 \), \( S(1, 3) = 0 \)

Using these relations, we compute the values step-by-step up to \( n = 10 \):

\[
\begin{aligned}
&n = 1: & S(1, 1) &= 2, & S(1, 2) &= 0, & S(1, 3) &= 0 & \text{Total} &= 2 \\
&n = 2: & S(2, 1) &= 2, & S(2, 2) &= 2, & S(2, 3) &= 0 & \text{Total} &= 4 \\
&n = 3: & S(3, 1) &= 4, & S(3, 2) &= 2, & S(3, 3) &= 2 & \text{Total} &= 8 \\
&n = 4: & S(4, 1) &= 8, & S(4, 2) &= 4, & S(4, 3) &= 2 & \text{Total} &= 14 \\
&n = 5: & S(5, 1) &= 14, & S(5, 2) &= 8, & S(5, 3) &= 4 & \text{Total} &= 26 \\
&n = 6: & S(6, 1) &= 26, & S(6, 2) &= 14, & S(6, 3) &= 8 & \text{Total} &= 48 \\
&n = 7: & S(7, 1) &= 48, & S(7, 2) &= 26, & S(7, 3) &= 14 & \text{Total} &= 88 \\
&n = 8: & S(8, 1) &= 88, & S(8, 2) &= 48, & S(8, 3) &= 26 & \text{Total} &= 162 \\
&n = 9: & S(9, 1) &= 162, & S(9, 2) &= 88, & S(9, 3) &= 48 & \text{Total} &= 298 \\
&n = 10: & S(10, 1) &= 298, & S(10, 2) &= 162, & S(10, 3) &= 88 & \text{Total} &= 548 \\
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, the number of valid 10-letter strings is \(\boxed{548}\).
